messages:
julia: heads up — canary p99 for model-text-6x jumped from ~210ms -> ~720ms around 02:15 UTC after CUDA/driver roll. saw kernel-selection drift in the runtime logs. opening INF ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-3124

akshay: captured a CUPTI trace and kernel-selection table. short seqs (<=64) that used flash_attn_fused_v2 now choose triton_gemm_wrapper_v1. autotuner weights look different.

maria: nvidia-smi top of node looks normal (util ~55%) but memcopy activity spiked. also seeing a ton of KV cache evictions per request. logs:
```
[2026-03-10T02:15:12Z] kernel_selector: text-6x seq=32 batch=8 -> triton_gemm_wrapper_v1
[2026-03-10T02:15:12Z] kv_cache: evict count +4k reqs
```

perf-bot: perf job #8812 linked in INF-3124 — CI reproducer timed out, but local repro on p3.2xlarge shows 2.8x p99 for short sequences.

ryan: can we pin kernel heuristic to prefer fusion for seq<=64 as a mitigation? also suggest rollback of driver on canary nodes. I'll start a rollback plan.

sre-oncall: routed traffic off canary pool to baseline cluster at 02:22 UTC — monitoring for 30m.

akshay: quick bisect points at triton tuner commit 3f4b2a1 -> changed score weights for fused kernels. repro script:
```
./scripts/repro_kernel_choice.sh --model text-6x --seq 32 --batch 8 --profile
```
CUPTI snippet shows kernel launch mismatch and longer shared-mem allocs.

julia: notes — KV cache hit-rate dropped from 98% -> 64% during spike, looks like eviction cascade because GEMM path uses larger temp buffers which push early eviction. path change may be increasing mem pressure.

maria: temporary mitigation: lowering max_batch for short-seq route to 4 and forcing fused path on runtime config. deploying patch to canary group now :thumbsup:

ryan: plan: 1) rollback driver on canary to last-known-good; 2) update triton tuner weights to prefer fusion for short seqs; 3) run controlled A/B with the repro harness; 4) follow up in INF-3124. tagging perf team.

akshay: leaving trace at /tmp/trace-1868001234.cupti and kernel table dump at /tmp/kernel-table-1868001234.log :eyes:
